_comment: Ruleset 4 of 5 — Branch naming, enforced by the server.
This is the remote half of scripts/checks/check-branch-name.sh. Until now
the convention lived in a git hook, which means it was enforced exactly as
well as each contributor's 'bash scripts/install-hooks.sh' — that is, not at
all for anyone who skipped it, or for any push made from the web UI.
THE PATTERN
<type>/<short-description>, where type is one of the Conventional Commit
types plus the release-train prefixes, exactly as CONTRIBUTING.md and the
local hook define them.
WHY THE AUTOMATION PREFIXES ARE EXCLUDED RATHER THAN MATCHED
dependabot/** , arena/** and friends are long, machine-generated and not
ours to rename. Excluding them in `conditions` keeps the human rule narrow
enough to be readable in the Rules UI. Anything newly introduced by a bot
needs its prefix added to `exclude` — otherwise its pushes are rejected,
which is a noisy, confusing failure for everyone involved.
(Main, release/** and hotfix/** cannot match the pattern either, because
those words are not in the type list; they are excluded explicitly so the
intent survives a later widening of the pattern.)
THIS IS THE MOST OPINIONATED RULESET IN THE SET
It rejects a push. A contributor who typed 'my-branch' gets a GitHub error
page mentioning a ruleset, not a friendly message, so the local hook and
CONTRIBUTING.md stay the primary teacher. If the friction is ever judged
too high for a first-time contributor, set "enforcement": "disabled" in
this file and re-run apply.sh — do not delete the file, or the decision
disappears from the history.
name: Branch naming
